LESSON: RESPONSIBILITY CHRISTIAN

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Trust By the end of the Sub strand, the learner ● Learners to read Proverbs 11:1
Topic 4.5: Responsibility Christian

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Responsibility Christian. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Explain the main ideas in Responsibility Christian
2. Practise Responsibility Christian at school and at home
3. Give Kenyan examples connected to Responsibility Christian

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Explain the main ideas in Responsibility Christian
   In simple words: practise until you can explain the main ideas in Responsibility Christian. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. Practise Responsibility Christian at school and at home
   In simple words: practise until you can practise Responsibility Christian at school and at home. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

3. Give Kenyan examples connected to Responsibility Christian
   In simple words: practise until you can give Kenyan examples connected to Responsibility Christian. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Responsibility Christian using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Responsibility Christian in the examples.
2. Explain Responsibility Christian to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Responsibility Christian.
4. Practise one skill from this lesson with a friend.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Responsibility Christian using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Responsibility Christian important for a Grade 3 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.
